_description: A USB data-line protector on a 30 x 15 mm two-layer board: J1 (4-pin header in), U1 (ESDA6V1BC6, a four-channel TVS array: the KiCad library's own symbol and SOT-23-6 footprint), J2 (4-pin header out). Both headers carry D+, GND, D-, VBUS on pins 1-4; each data line flows through U1, D+ in on pin 1 and out on pin 6, D- on 3 and 4, a TVS channel to ground at each, and both COM pins (2 and 5), which the part joins inside, are on GND. Tracks 0.25 mm on KiCad's default rules. It passes kicad-cli pcb drc at every severity with nothing unconnected, carries the library's pin names on every pad, and runs VBUS and GND at 0.5 A. Its schematic, esd_guard.kicad_sch, is the same circuit on KiCad's stock symbols, every footprint on the board linked to its symbol: it passes kicad-cli sch erc at every severity and matches the board exactly. The project's own sym-lib-table and fp-lib-table name the pack's own copies of the stock entries the board and schematic were drawn from (selftest/assets/lib, through ${KIPRJMOD}/lib), so DRC and ERC read the same library on every host, configured or not, KiCad 9 or 10. selftest/assets/make_baseline.py made all of it, and says how; make_libraries.py the copies. selftest/assets/kicad10/ is the same project as KiCad 10.0.8 saved it, its tables naming the copies one directory up, and reader.kicad_pcb a reader fixture with inner layers, a stated stackup, every via kind, a filled pour and a keep-out (make_kicad10.py): no gate's baseline reads them. vbus_droop.cir models the VBUS path from the host through the cable and the board to J2 under a 0.5 A step, and dips to 4.83 V against USB 2.0's 4.75 V. esd_guard.kicad_dru holds one custom rule (usb_pair: the data pair at least 0.2 mm wide), which the 0.25 mm tracks keep and pcb.drc's probes show live; esd_guard.symbols.json is the statement pcb.schematic_from_board writes the same circuit from. esda6v1bc6_land.json is ST's recommended SOT23-6L land, numbered by function, which KiCad's SOT-23-6 fits to 0.0125 mm. power_board.kicad_pcb (make_power_board.py) is a second board, placed and netted but not routed, that only the battery rules, pcb.mismate and pcb.usbc_receptacle read, with its schematic, power_board.kicad_sch (make_power_schematic.py), beside it, where pcb.charge_temperature reads the NTC's symbol: a USB-C receptacle in, a sink with 5.1k on each CC pin, an MCP73833-AMI/UN charger with its THERM on an NTC and PROG on 3k, a PTC between the cell's connector BT1 and VSYS, a one-cell protector sensing the cell through the PTC and 330 ohm and driving a dual N-MOSFET in the cell's negative lead, a wire out, and two 8-position FFC housings joined by a flex that a 6-way cable also fits, two positions either way, never putting VBUS on GND. enclosure.step is a closed 2 mm box around the populated board, its lid 2.365 mm over the header pins, its frame's origin on the cavity floor under the board's corner, so the board sits 4 mm up; the footprints' 3D models are KiCad's own, kept in selftest/assets/3d/ so the fit sees the same parts on every host. radio_board.kicad_pcb (make_radio_board.py) is a third board, 45 x 30 mm on four copper layers, that only pcb.antenna_keepout reads: KiCad's stock ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 turned 90 degrees with its antenna on the board's left edge, a 0603 capacitor 2.6 mm outside the keep-out, a header at the far edge, and a GND pour on each layer, filled by KiCad, its outline 0.85 mm clear of the keep-out.

_claims.statement: Every part on the populated board keeps at least 1.0 mm from the enclosure, and nothing collides with it

main.source: a one-cell pack on an LG INR18650 MJ1 cell, its protection board in the pack and a two-wire pigtail to BT1. LG Chem product specification LRB-PS-CY3500_MJ1, rev 1, 2016-06-30, read 2026-11-24: 2.4 max charge voltage 4.2 +- 0.05 V (upper_charge_v 4.25), 2.5 max charge current 1.0 C, 3350 mA, 2.6 end voltage (cut off) 2.5 V, 2.9 charge 0 ~ 45 C. short_a is a fixture estimate, not measured: the cell (4.2.1: at most 40 mOhm initial AC impedance), the pack's FETs and the pigtail in series, 10 A at the least and 40 A at the most

charger.source: Microchip MCP73833/4 datasheet DS22005B (2009), read 2026-11-24: THERM is pin 8 of the MSOP-10 (KiCad's MCP73833-xxx-UN symbol); VREG 4.168-4.232 V for the 4.20 V option; IREG = 1000 V / RPROG, 900-1100 mA at PROG 1.0 kOhm (k_v 900-1100 V); ITHERM 47-53 uA, VT1 1.20-1.26 V, VT2 0.235-0.265 V; the AMI option is 4.20 V with its timer disabled (0 hours). R3 is 1 %. TH1 is a fixture NTC, 10 kOhm +- 1 %, B25/85 4250 K +- 1 %, not a product's

protector.source: fixture values, not a product's: a one-cell protector on KiCad's AP9101CK symbol pins (VM 1, VDD 2, VSS 3, DO 4, CO 5), overcharge detection 4.35 V at the most, overdischarge detection 2.85 V at the least; VDD through F1 and R5 (330 ohm) from the cell; DO and CO on the gates of Q1 (KiCad's FDS6890A symbol: S1 1, G1 2, S2 3, G2 4), whose sources sit on the cell's negative and on ground

pack_pcm.source: fixture values, not a product's: the pack's own protection board, overcharge 4.30 V at the most, overdischarge 2.30 V at the least, as a pack drawing would state them

fuse.source: fixture values, not a product's: a PTC that holds 0.5 A, trips by 1.0 A, trips within 0.1 s at 8 A, and breaks 80 A

wire_out.source: 26 AWG solid copper, 0.405 mm across, 0.129 mm^2 (ASTM B258), PVC insulated: 70 C in service and 160 C its short-circuit limit (IEC 60364-5-54's k = 115 pair); continuous_a 1.0 A is a fixture rating, not a standard's

flex.source: fixture: an 8-way FFC from J10 to J11, contacts on the same side at both ends, so position n meets position n. A 6-way FFC of the same 0.5 mm pitch also seats in the 8-way housings, anywhere in their two spare positions; it cannot go in reversed (one contact side) and the other contact type is not stocked for it

cell.source: fixture: the pack's pigtail ends in the keyed housing that mates BT1, and the pack drawing fixes which wire is on which contact, so it cannot meet BT1 reversed

usb_in.source: USB Type-C Cable and Connector Specification R2.0: the plug meets the receptacle in either orientation and both are correct matings (the receptacle carries both rows); no other plug fits the receptacle

wire.source: fixture: the lead is soldered into J6 once, at assembly, and checked there; it is never plugged

usb_in.source: fixture: J1 is a sink terminated by R1 and R2 (5.1k, 1 % fixture parts) from CC1 and CC2 to GND, with USB 2.0 data on both rows. It never reads the source's advertisement: U1 draws at most 1100 V / 3 kOhm = 0.367 A (MCP73833 DS22005B, IREG = 1000 V / RPROG, k 900-1100 V), inside USB 2.0's default 500 mA, so Table 4-25's +-20 % Rd applies

radio.source: KiCad 9.0.9's stock RF_Module:ESP32-S3-WROOM-1, whose rule area is the module's keep-out; the gate finds the module by its library alone, and the record names the board it sits on

_notes._claims: the claim the baseline was calibrated against. pcb.enclosure_fit reads its limit from the claim tagged enclosure-fit (ctx.acceptance): the least gap a part keeps from the enclosure, in mm, >=. 1.0 mm is a common allowance for print and assembly tolerance. The baseline's nearest part, a header, is 2.365 mm under the lid, and raised_board's headers run 0.64 mm into it. Until general-packs P7 the limit was pcb_enclosure_clearance_mm, a pack parameter; a project that still states it is refused, and the error names the move.
_notes._units: Millimetres for every length (KiCad's file unit), amperes, degrees C of rise above ambient, ounces of copper per square foot (1 oz = 35 um = 1.378 mil).
_notes._paths: pcb_board, pcb_spice_deck and pcb_enclosure_step resolve against the PROJECT ROOT (ctx.root). Its project file (.kicad_pro), custom rules (.kicad_dru) and schematic (.kicad_sch, with every sheet under it) when they exist beside it with the same name, and the project's sym-lib-table and fp-lib-table, go with it to kicad-cli: they hold the design rules, KiCad's ERC and DRC exclusions and the libraries.
_notes.pcb_board: The board this pack checks. One board per project projection; a project with two boards scopes the key (pcb.pcb_board) per model, or runs two projects.
_notes.pcb_net_currents_a: {net: amperes} for every net whose current matters. pcb.net_width judges only the nets named here, because the board does not say what flows where. 0.5 A on VBUS and GND is a USB 2.0 port's budget. A net may instead take a route: {amps, from, to, rest_a}, two pads as REF.PAD: its tracks on a route of the copper between them are judged at amps, every other track at rest_a (default amps, never above it), so a return net shared by a cell and a small part's fan-out is not judged at the cell's current on every stub.
_notes.pcb_temp_rise_limit_c: How far above ambient a track may run, degrees C. 10 C is the common design choice and the bottom of IPC-2221's fitted range (10-100 C): below it the formula is extrapolation, and the verdict says so.
_notes.pcb_copper_oz_outer: Copper weight of the outer layers. 1 oz is what a fab quotes without being asked; the gate uses that and says '[pack default]' when this key is absent.
_notes.pcb_copper_oz_inner: Copper weight of inner layers, 0.5 oz by the same convention; the gate says '[pack default]' when this key is absent. Unused on this two-layer board.
_notes.pcb_drc_severity: all (the default), error or warning. 'all' because a check at error severity cannot see a warning, and the fab still prints the silk a warning is about. Waive a finding by excluding it in KiCad, which records it in the .kicad_pro: never by narrowing this.
_notes.pcb_drc_timeout_s: Wall clock for one kicad-cli run. This board takes well under a second, a 4-layer board of about a hundred footprints about 2 s; 120 s is for a hang, which reads as a skip.
_notes.pcb_erc_severity: all (the default), error or warning, for pcb.erc, by the same reasoning as pcb_drc_severity. The schematic is the board's name with .kicad_sch (KiCad's rule for a project's root schematic) unless pcb_schematic names another for ERC; pcb.parity always compares with the board's own, as KiCad does.
_notes.pcb_fab: The fab whose published limits pcb.fab_rules holds the board to: jlcpcb (gates/fab/jlcpcb.json, each number quoted from its capability page with the day it was read), or a path from the project root to a fab file of the same shape. The row is chosen, in the service pcb_fab_service names, by the board's copper layer count and pcb_copper_oz_outer.
_notes.pcb_fab_service: Which of the fab file's services the board is ordered on: each service lists the dielectrics and via kinds it builds, and a board whose stackup names another dielectric, or that holds another via kind, skips rather than be judged on that service's rows. It may be left out when the file has one service; with several and none named, the gate skips, naming them. standard is JLCPCB's FR-4 service with through vias; this board states no stackup, so it is KiCad's default FR4.
_notes.pcb_spice_deck: The SPICE deck pcb.spice runs with ngspice -b, from the project root. The deck is the project's model of the circuit, not the board: ngspice solves what it says. Relative .include and .lib paths resolve from the deck's directory.
_notes.pcb_spice_measure: The .meas result the verdict reads (ngspice lowercases names; so does the gate).
_notes.pcb_spice_min: The lowest value that passes, in pcb_spice_units. 4.75 V is USB 2.0's minimum VBUS at a high-power port's device connector. pcb_spice_max is the highest; give either or both.
_notes.pcb_spice_units: The measure's units, as ngspice computes it (SI: V, A, s). Stated by the project, because the gate cannot tell which quantity a .meas measures.
_notes.pcb_spice_timeout_s: Wall clock for one ngspice run. The baseline deck solves in about 0.01 s.
_notes.pcb_enclosure_step: The enclosure's solid (its walls and lid, the material, not the cavity) as a STEP file in mm, from the project root. The baseline's is a closed box made by selftest/assets/make_enclosure.py around the populated baseline board.
_notes.pcb_board_placement: Where the board sits in the enclosure's frame: turned rot_x_deg about x, then rot_y_deg about y, then rot_z_deg about z (each about the enclosure's own axes, through the board's origin: one 3x3 rotation, so face down is rot_x_deg 180 and on its edge is 90), then moved by x, y, z mm. x, y and z must be stated; a rotation not stated is 0. Here the board sits 4 mm above the cavity floor, upright. The board's own frame is kicad-cli's STEP export with --user-origin 0x0mm: the board file's (0, 0) at the origin, x right, y up (KiCad's y negated), z up from the board's bottom face.
_notes.pcb_enclosure_bodiless: References of placed parts that have no body to fit (an antenna drawn in copper): each listed is a statement that the fit need not see it. Every other SMD or through-hole part, and every footprint that shows a 3D model whatever its type, must name a 3D model that kicad-cli finds, or have a height in pcb_part_heights_mm, or pcb.enclosure_fit skips, naming it.
_notes.pcb_part_heights_mm: {ref: {h, source, box_mm | circle_mm | polygon_mm, lead_mm}} for a placed part whose 3D model is not on this host (none named, or one found nowhere here): its courtyard's box on its own side, or one outline in the footprint's own frame (box_mm [[x0, y0], [x1, y1]], circle_mm {center: [x, y], d} for a round part, polygon_mm [[x, y], ...]), raised h mm from the board (a datasheet's seated height), stands in for its body, the model left out of the staged copy; a through-hole part also gets a cylinder in each plated hole, the drill wide, to lead_mm past the board's far face (2.5 mm unstated, named in the verdict). On a host that has the model, the model is fitted and the height is named unused: one body each. The box is written as the part's model, so kicad-cli seats, turns and flips it as it does any model. A part with no courtyard and no outline is refused. Not used here: both footprints carry KiCad's own models.
_notes.pcb_model_dirs: {variable: folder}: the folder a 3D model path variable stands for, from the project root or absolute ({"KICAD9_3DMODEL_DIR": "hardware/3dmodels"}, or a variable of the project's own). A model naming the variable is looked for in that folder alone, and the staged board names the folder in the variable's place, so kicad-cli reads the file the fit found. The gate reads no environment variable: a 3D library outside KiCad's own install folders is stated here, in the key. KIPRJMOD (the board's folder) is refused. Not used here: both footprints name their models through ${KIPRJMOD}.
_notes.pcb_enclosure_contacts: {ref: {feature: {reason, region_mm}}}: a part that touches one feature of the enclosure by design (a switch on its plunger, a receptacle in its cutout, a light pipe, a cell on foam). A feature is a region of the enclosure, region_mm [[x0, y0, z0], [x1, y1, z1]] in its frame, or one shape of another board in the same enclosure, '<fit>:<ref>' or '<fit>:board' (pcb_enclosure_fits only). The part's distance to that feature is listed and left out of its clearance; against everything else it keeps the limit, and any shared volume still fails. A ref with no feature, a feature with no reason, and a region that holds the whole enclosure are refused: an entry for one part against anything once hid a real interference. Not used here.
_notes.pcb_enclosure_fits: {id: {board, enclosure_step, placement, bodiless, contacts, heights}} for several boards: each entry one board in its enclosure, its fields as the singular keys above (board as pcb_board). Boards that name the same enclosure file are fitted against each other too: a part of one keeps the limit from every shape of another, the bodies included, and a shared volume fails. The verdict is the worst over every board. It replaces the singular keys (pcb_enclosure_step, pcb_board_placement, pcb_enclosure_bodiless, pcb_enclosure_contacts, pcb_part_heights_mm): stating both is refused. Not used here: one board.
_notes.pcb_fit_timeout_s: Wall clock for each child of the fit (the STEP export, the regions' pass, the geometry), each. Unstated, it is 120 s and 5 s for each part the child handles: a populated handheld board of 74 parts took 2 to 4 minutes. The baseline takes about 1 s and 3 s; 120 s is stated here for a hang.
_notes.pcb_pin_names_ignore: Pin names pcb.pin_names never compares: unused-pin names, which may sit on any net, and KiCad's hidden-name placeholder. Every other repeated name must carry one net.
_notes.pcb_pin_names_series: {ref: {pairs: [[pin, pin]], source}}: on that ref, each pair is the two ends of one series element that the library names alike (an EMI filter array names both ends of a channel CH1), so it may carry two nets. A pair must name the only two pins of the ref that carry its name, or the gate errors: the record is for another design. A pair stated on one ref clears nothing on another. Empty here: the ESD array's two COM pins are one node inside the part, not a series pair.
_notes.pcb_land_drawings: {ref: drawing record} for pcb.land_pattern, each a JSON file from the project root: {part, source, view: "top", y_axis: "up" (as printed) or "down" (as a KiCad footprint), pads: [{number, function, x, y, w, h}]} in mm. The baseline holds U1 to ST's recommended SOT23-6L land; KiCad's SOT-23-6 fits it to 0.0125 mm.
_notes.pcb_batteries: {id: record}, one per battery (an object keyed by id, not a list: the mutation walk reaches an object's leaves, and other records point at the ids). Each: board (else pcb_board); terminals {ref, value, pos, neg, therm (the pack's thermistor pin, or null), taps (for two or more cells in series, the junction pins from the lowest up)}; chemistry (li-ion, li-polymer, lifepo4, lto, nimh, li-primary or alkaline: it picks which rules apply, never a number); series and parallel (whole numbers); cell, each value per cell from the cell's datasheet: upper_charge_v (a rechargeable cell's upper limit charging voltage, with its tolerance), open_circuit_v (a primary cell's fresh open-circuit voltage: a primary cell has no charge voltage), discharge_v_min, charge_a_max, charge_temp_c [lo, hi] (the widest window any charge is allowed in) and short_a [least, most] or internal_resistance_ohm [least, most]; ntc (the pack's NTC: r25_ohm, r25_tol_pct, beta_tol_pct (with a table too: state 0 only for an exact table), and rt_table_c_ohm [[C, ohm], ...] or beta_k and beta_pair_c); source. Every key of cell is optional ("cell": {} states a cell nobody has chosen); a rule that needs a value the record lacks errors, naming the key quoted, unless something it judges without the value fails first. references/battery.md ('Every field') marks each record's required keys. The baseline's records name power_board.kicad_pcb, a board only the tier-0 battery, mis-mating and USB-C rules read.
_notes.pcb_protectors: {id: record}, one per protecting element, holding every function it serves. Each: battery (an id in pcb_batteries); kind (charger, protector, pack-pcm, bms, gauge, fuse, ptc, efuse or blocking: a charger stops its own charge, every other kind says how it acts); where (board, in-pack or firmware: an in-pack element counts on its datasheet's word, firmware is named and never counted); board, ref and value when on the board; functions, any of: charge_v {v_reg_v [min, max] or divider {vfb_v, top_ref, bottom_ref, tol_pct}, per_cell, set_by}, charge_a {a_max, or prog {ref, k_v [min, max], r_tol_pct}, set_by}, charge_temp {sense {pin, kind current with i_a, cold_v, hot_v, or kind ratio with pullup_ref, pullup_tol_pct, cold_frac, hot_frac}, ntc {ref, value, r25_ohm, r25_tol_pct, beta_tol_pct, and rt_table_c_ohm or beta_k and beta_pair_c} or {battery_therm: true}, network {series_ref, parallel_ref, tol_pct, others}, acts {pin, to {ref, pin}}; in the pack: window_c {cold_c, hot_c}; a charger may give sense {pin} alone, with no ntc, to be judged only on whether its input is switched off}, overcharge_v {v_max, per_cell, sense, acts}, overdischarge_v {v_min, per_cell, sense {pin, through [refs]} or {taps}, acts {pin, switch {ref, value, control, path}}}, trip {kind fuse, ptc, fet, efuse or pcm, terminal pos or neg, path_pins or switch, hold_a, trip_a, trip_max_s [[A, s]], interrupt_a, ahead [{ref, value, why}]}, reverse_block {terminal pos or neg, path_pins [p, q] or switch {ref, value, path}, through [{ref, value, path [p, q], why}] (the series parts from the terminal to the block, in order: a power switch), ahead [{ref, value, why}]} (read by pcb.mismate only), safety_timer (evidence only); source. A field shown as [min, max] (and i_a, cold_v, hot_v, cold_frac, hot_frac, vfb_v, window_c's cold_c and hot_c) is the datasheet range and refuses one number. A field that takes one number takes the datasheet's guaranteed bound on the side that protects less, never its typical, and the rule cannot tell the two apart: v_max is the most overcharge detection voltage, v_min the least overdischarge detection voltage, a_max the most charge current, trip_a the current by which the part is sure to trip, trip_max_s the longest time at each current, interrupt_a the current it is rated to break.
_notes.pcb_conductors: {id: record}, each a conductor a cell can drive a fault through: battery; board; kind (wire, ffc, contact or track); for a track, net and continuous_rise_c (its rating is IPC-2221 at that rise, on its narrowest stretch); otherwise ref, value, pins (all on one net), area_mm2 of ONE conductor (parallel contacts get no credit) and continuous_a; start_c (its temperature in service) and limit_c (what its insulation allows in a fault); protected_by (the protector ids that guard it, each stating a trip; [] when nothing does, judged against IEC 62368-1's PS1 15 W and the conductor's own rating); source. pcb.fault_current turns on limit_c and continuous_a: say where each comes from.
_notes.pcb_matings: {id: record}, each a connector and what meets it: a {board, ref, value}; b, another connector {board, ref, value}, a battery's pigtail {battery: id} (a must then be the battery's own connector) or {external: what lies outside every board here}; map (straight, reversed, or {a_pin: b_pin}), for two connectors only; modes, the wrong ways it can meet: reversed, rotate (a two-row header turned 180 degrees), flipped_type (the other FFC contact type), {narrower: N} (an N-way cable in the housings), {offset: k} or {offset: k, rows: 2} (a's unshrouded header off by up to k positions or columns), {slide: [a's pins, the deepest first]} (an audio plug passing a's contacts), {bridges: [[pin, pin]]} (a wrong plug shorting a's contacts); a battery takes reversed, and cell_reversed (one loose cell of two or more in series turned in its holder: counted when a current runs through it backwards, from three or more in series, a second string or a charger, since no board element blocks it; two alone cancel), an external side bridges only; [] says nothing else meets it, with why in source; source. The power rules join the two connectors' nets, so an element on another board counts. pcb.mismate requires modes, and a mating naming every connector that carries a source (here: the flex, the cell's housing, the USB-C receptacle and the wire).
_notes.pcb_usbc: {id: record}, one per USB-C receptacle: board; ref and value; role (sink, source or drp); usb2 (true when it carries USB 2.0 data); pins ({Type-C pin: pad}, only for a footprint that does not number its pads A1..B12); then by role: a sink's reads_rp (true when it reads the source's advertisement to draw more than default power: Rd +-10 %, else +-20 %) and cc_resistor_tol_pct; a source's rp {current default, 1.5A or 3A, rail_v 5 or 3.3, rail (the net it pulls up to)}, cc_resistor_tol_pct and vbus_switch {ref, value, path [pin, pin]}; a DRP's vbus_switch; or, for any role, cc_by {ref, value, pins {CC1, CC2}} for a controller whose pins terminate CC, with others [{ref, value, why}] for a resistor beside it that carries no termination; source. The bands are gates/usbc.json's, from the Type-C specification's Tables 4-24 and 4-25.
_notes.pcb_rails: {id: record}, each a net a regulator or an outside supply drives: board; net; nominal_v; return (its return net); source. pcb.mismate reads each as a source: two the nominal map joins at one nominal voltage are one rail. A net a cell drives is the battery's and is not stated again here. Empty here: the power board carries no regulator.
_notes.pcb_antennas: {id: record}, one per radio part whose antenna keep-out pcb.antenna_keepout judges, beside the RF_Module footprints it finds by itself on pcb_board and on each board a record names: board (else pcb_board); ref and value (held to the board); keepout: "footprint" (the part's own rule area), "none" (no antenna on the board: one on a cable, a u.FL or an SMA; listed, not judged), {"drawing": path} (the vendor's drawing in pcb_land_drawings' shape plus keepout {polygon [[x, y], ...]} in its frame, registered on the footprint by three or more numbered pads, not all on one line) or {"rule_area": name} (a keep-out rule area the designer drew on the board and named, such as a chip antenna's clearance), {"rule_area": {"uuid": id}} (one rule area by its id) or {"rule_area": {"covers": ref}} (every rule area whose outline holds a point of that part's copper); own_nets (optional: a printed antenna's own nets, its feed and ground arm, whose tracks reaching the part's pads are its own copper, listed and not counted); source. Each keep-out is judged on every copper layer, as stored and as refilled. Here: U1 on radio_board.kicad_pcb, by its footprint's own area, which KiCad's library draws on F.Cu, In1.Cu and B.Cu only.
